report:
Reviewed the complete expansion dependency claim and all six ordinary implementation entries. The claim permits parsed identities, macro resolution and definitions, generated output, and completeness facts, and prohibits dependence on checked item signatures, trait solutions, or function bodies. local_expanded_module_items in local_syms/mods.rs reads unexpanded identities and dispatches item variants. Nonmacro items use syntactic attributes and are converted to symbols, with active attributes withheld. Bang expansion resolves only a macro definition and parses its output; depth/failure handling does not invoke semantic checking. Completeness helpers use the same expansion outcomes, syntactic attributes and derive identities; comparing a target trait identity is not trait solving.

The newly associated check/resolve/mod.rs macro constructor uses a module scope and empty ribs. Its lookup path reads names, namespaces, imports and expanded child identities, handles cyclic imports, and resolves metadata export edges; it never requests a checked signature, body or trait solution. symbol/mod.rs supplies identity-only name/module/child dispatch and MacroDefSymbol::expand. The latter reads macro definition tokens or calls external bang expansion, which are expressly permitted macro inputs, not function bodies. Its separate FnSymbol/TraitSymbol semantic methods are not invoked by expansion. local_syms/macro_invocations.rs parses invocation tokens against the selected definition, returns an error item on failure, and parses generated source. derive.rs keys expansion by item and macro identity and occurrence, then parses generated text in the source scope. derive/builtins.rs constructs supported Clone output from syntactic field names and shape; checking whether generic/where-clause syntax is present does not lower signatures or solve obligations. Unsupported forms return None. Generated clone method text is output syntax, not a checked function body dependency. These helpers now carry associations so their changes require a fresh review.

The complete associated test set contains only sage_meta::todo::modules_expand_dependencies. It has no assertions and establishes no runtime property. Its explicit deferred matrix calls for cold/warm expansion traces, invalidation when invocation or selected macro output changes, noninvalidation for body-only/unrelated-signature edits, and backdating equal reconstructed output before downstream consumers execute. This is an honest accepted test deferral, not successful coverage: completing it requires controlled incremental revisions and observable query execution at the expansion boundary, with positive and negative assertions for the described scenarios. In particular this review does not claim that broad syntactic CST reads have proved optimal invalidation. The source-level prohibition on checked semantic detail is supported by the inspected call paths; the runtime dependency/invalidation matrix remains visibly TODO. No N/A or implementation TODO entry is present.

Executed cargo fmt, cargo build (passed with existing warnings), and cargo test -p sage-meta --test semantic_spec todo::modules_expand_dependencies -- --exact (one placeholder test passed; not behavioral verification). Performed a fresh start after association edits and captured supporting decision policy and module reexport context through review read. No production behavior or tests were changed. Central delegated code-quality and Sage-sanity checks are coordinated by root for the comment-only edits.
